messages.subject: storable votes model in Stan
parts:
Assuming I understood the discussion in Gelman and Hill's
applied regression book (p. 122) on the different parameterizations,
here's a translation of the storable votes model into Stan,
using Andrew's preferred parameterization with the cuts
on the same scale as the data and sigma the scale of the logistic
noise.

data {
int<lower=2> K; // num ordered outcomes
int<lower=0> N; // num games
int<lower=1> J; // num players
int<lower=1,upper=J> jj[N]; // player for game n
real x[N]; // payoff for game n
int<lower=1,upper=K> y[N]; // initial votes for game n
}
parameters {
ordered[K-1] c[J]; // data scale cuts for player j
real mu_c[K-1]; // mean cutpoints
real<lower=0> sigma_c[K-1]; // cutpoint scales
real mu_lsc; // mean log(sigma_c)
real<lower=0> sigma_lsc; // scale of log(sigma_c)
real<lower=0> sigma; // logistic outcome scale
}
model {
mu_lsc ~ cauchy(0,25);
sigma_lsc ~ cauchy(0,25);
for (k in 1:(K-1)) {
mu_c[k] ~ cauchy(0,25);
sigma_c[k] ~ lognormal(mu_lsc, sigma_lsc);
for (j in 1:J)
c[j,k] ~ normal(mu_c[k],sigma_c[k]);
}
sigma ~ cauchy(0,25);
for (n in 1:N)
y[n] ~ ordered_logistic(x[n] / sigma, sigma * c[jj[n]]);
}

This is a direct translation with very diffuse priors (Cauchy
and half-Cauchy).

Someone should check my work in the translation.

The Stan model with a regression coefficient beta and
letting the cutpoints take their own scale is simpler
to write down:

y[n] ~ ordered_logistic(beta * x[n], c[jj[n]]);

And then beta gets a diffuse prior and sigma goes away.
You could then define the parameters Andrew likes as:

sigma <- 1 / beta;
cuts_on_data_scale <- c * beta;

- Bob
